method: WebFetch, WebSearch and curl. The USCIS fee schedule (Form G-1055, edition 10/01/26) and the Home Office 'Biometric enrolment: policy guidance' v14.0 (published for staff 4 June 2026) were downloaded and read locally with pdftotext. irishimmigration.ie pages were fetched with curl and read as text. travel.state.gov and usembassy.gov refused automated fetch (HTTP 403 / Cloudflare block); figures from them are taken from search-engine summaries of those pages and are marked secondhand. Nothing is from memory.

appointments.application: US nonimmigrant visa (from abroad), e.g. B-1/B-2, F-1, or O-1/H-1B after USCIS approves the I-129 petition
appointments.authority: US Department of State, Bureau of Consular Affairs (embassy or consulate)
appointments.waived: Since 2025-10-01 (update dated 2025-09-18) all nonimmigrant applicants, including under-14s and over-79s, generally need an in-person interview. Waivers may still be granted only for A-1, A-2, C-3 (most), G-1 to G-4, NATO-1 to NATO-6, TECRO E-1, diplomatic/official-type visas, and renewals of a full-validity B-1, B-2, B1/B2 or Border Crossing Card within 12 months of the prior visa's expiry where the applicant was at least 18 at the prior issuance. A consular officer can still require an interview.
appointments.feeBasis: No separate interview fee: the interview is booked with the MRV (visa application) fee. 'Non-petition-based nonimmigrant visas (except E category) cost $185.00, while petition-based visa categories cost $205.00' (H, L, O, P, Q, R). Fee in force since 2023-06-17.
appointments.missed: MRV fee receipts paid on or after 2022-10-01 are 'valid for 365 days from the date a receipt is issued'; the applicant must schedule an interview (or submit an interview waiver application) within that period, but the interview need not happen within it. Cancelling or rescheduling in the same country is free through the appointment website. A missed appointment without cancellation is recorded as a no-show; the fee is not refunded (secondhand: some posts then require a new DS-160, a new fee and a new booking).
appointments.note: travel.state.gov (interview waiver update 2025-09-18; Fees for Visa Services; Global Visa Wait Times) and the embassy FAQ pages (do.usembassy.gov, mk.usembassy.gov) returned 403; every figure here is from search summaries of those official pages. Wait times are published per post (travel.state.gov/.../wait-times.html, 'measured from fee payment to interview date', updated monthly) and vary by post, so no single leadDays. The O-1 USCIS page says only: 'Once we approve your petition, you can apply for your visa at a U.S. Embassy or Consulate.' fee=185 is the non-petition class; an O-1/H-1B applicant pays 205. Whether the H.R. 1 Visa Integrity Fee (USD 250) is being collected was not confirmed (see research-entry.json).

appointments.application: Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (green card, inside the US)
appointments.waived: USCIS may reuse previously collected biometrics at its discretion; USCIS 'has general authority to require and collect biometrics from any applicant'. No general waiver read.
appointments.feeBasis: No separate biometric services fee for I-485. G-1055 edition 10/01/26 lists the I-485 general filing fee as 'Paper Filing: $1,440 Online Filing: $1,390' (under-14 filing with a parent: paper $950, online $900) with no biometric line; the separate 'DHS Biometric Services Fee' survives only for some forms (EOIR-40, EOIR-42A, EOIR-42B at '$30 per person'; I-821 TPS: 'You must submit the biometric services fee separately from the filing fee').
appointments.missed: Reschedule through the USCIS online account 'before the date and time of the original appointment, and you must establish good cause' (requests at least 12 hours before). If you miss it, 'USCIS may consider your application, petition, or request abandoned and it may be denied.' Policy Manual Vol. 1 Part C Ch. 2: under 8 CFR 103.2(b)(13)(ii) a case is 'considered abandoned and denied if the alien fails to appear for a biometric services appointment' unless a timely address change or rescheduling request was received; an after-the-date request can be made only to the USCIS Contact Center, and USCIS 'may, in its discretion' consider whether the request was abandoned.
appointments.note: Appointment notice is Form I-797C, which 'will include the date, time, and location for your ASC appointment'. Neither the USCIS page nor the Policy Manual chapter says how many days ahead the notice is sent, so leadDays is null. Good cause examples in the Policy Manual: medical needs, planned travel, major life events, transport barriers, work conflicts, late-delivered notices. Fee schedule: https://www.uscis.gov/g-1055 (PDF edition 10/01/26). Policy: https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-1-part-c-chapter-2

appointments.application: Form I-129 O-1 petition (employer/agent files for the beneficiary)
appointments.waived: Not required as a petition step: the USCIS O-1 page does not mention biometrics or an ASC appointment for the beneficiary. The beneficiary's fingerprints and photo are taken at the consular interview abroad after approval (see the US consular interview row).
appointments.feeBasis: G-1055 edition 10/01/26 lists no biometric services fee for I-129.
appointments.missed: Not applicable: no ASC appointment on the O-1 page.
appointments.note: Page quote: 'Once we approve your petition, you can apply for your visa at a U.S. Embassy or Consulate.' A change-of-status beneficiary inside the US was not covered by the page. missedOutcome is a placeholder because there is nothing to miss.

appointments.application: UK in-country applications for leave to remain / settlement / citizenship (biometric immigration document)
appointments.authority: Home Office, via UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS, run by Sopra Steria) or a Service and Support Centre (SSC)
appointments.waived: Not required where an exemption or exception applies, where officials reuse previously enrolled biometrics, or where the applicant used the UK Immigration: ID Check app. People physically unable to give fingerprints may be excused from fingerprints but must give a facial image.
appointments.feeBasis: gov.uk/ukvcas: 'How much you pay depends on the type of service point and whether you need extra services'; you 'can pay extra for: out of hours or weekend appointments, next day or same day appointments if your application is urgent'. gov.uk gives no amounts. Secondhand (law-firm guides): free appointments at core service points on weekdays 10:00-16:00; enhanced service points about GBP 69.99 per person in office hours.
appointments.missed: Home Office guidance: in-country applicants are told to 'make an appointment at a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) location within 45 working days' (or at an SSC within 15 working days). If they have not enrolled or booked in that period they get a rejection warning letter; 'If the person does not enrol or make an appointment after the further warning period of 10 days set out in the warning letter, you must reject their application.' Officials must not invalidate when the person books after the warning, unless they then fail to attend without 'a significant reason, such as a bereavement of an immediate family member or is hospitalised'. Sanctions: 'refuse or reject the immigration application (which includes treating the application as not being made)', vary or cancel existing leave, refuse to issue an eVisa, civil penalty (in-country only).
appointments.note: deadlineDays 45 is WORKING days, not calendar days (about 63 calendar days). Plus a 10-day warning period before rejection. Source: 'Biometric enrolment: policy guidance' version 14.0, published for Home Office staff 4 June 2026, pp. 7, 29, 31. Cost page: https://www.gov.uk/ukvcas. A rejected (invalid) application is treated as never made, which is worse than a refusal for someone whose leave depends on a pending in-time application.

appointments.authority: Home Office, via a commercial Visa Application Centre (VAC)
appointments.waived: Officials may exceptionally excuse or defer attendance at a VAC (medical cases, people unable to travel, senior foreign government officials, exceptional circumstances), or reuse previously enrolled biometrics, or the applicant may use the UK Immigration: ID Check app where offered.
appointments.feeBasis: No VAC appointment price read on gov.uk.
appointments.missed: Guidance: 'If a person does not comply with a requirement to enrol their biometrics, you must consider the circumstances of the case and whether the person had a reasonable excuse. Where you are satisfied that a person has failed to comply with the requirement, without a reasonable excuse, the Secretary of State may treat the application as not being made.' Officials 'must, in most circumstances, not consider an application until checks against the person's biometrics are completed'.
appointments.note: No overseas booking deadline is set in the guidance (the 45/15 working-day periods are in-country only). Biometrics are given 'as part of their application' at the VAC.

appointments.application: Canada visitor visa, study permit, work permit or permanent residence
appointments.authority: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), at a Visa Application Centre (VAC) or, in Canada, a designated Service Canada location
appointments.waived: Not required for some groups; US nationals are exempt from biometrics for work permits (see research-workpermission.json and canada.ca/.../biometrics/who-needs-to-give.html).
appointments.feeBasis: Separate fee paid when you apply: 'CAN$85' per person; families applying together pay a 'maximum total fee of CAN$170' (groups of 3+ performing artists: CAD 255 maximum, IRCC fee list). Appointments themselves 'are free to book' - 'Don't pay anyone for an appointment.'
appointments.missed: 'You have 30 days from the time you get your BIL to give your biometrics.' If you can't, 'use the web form to tell us why you need more time' (e.g. upload a screenshot of the earliest appointment confirmation). canada.ca: if your application 'has been refused because you didn't give biometrics', you can't give them unless you reapply, pay the fees including the biometrics fee, and get a new BIL; using an old BIL can mean 'delays in your application processing, or your application may be refused'.
appointments.note: Fee read on https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/campaigns/biometrics.html; 30 days and free booking read on the where-to-give page. The refusal wording comes from canada.ca search summaries (when-to-give-temporary-residence.html, visit-canada/after-apply-next-steps.html); the page fetch confirmed it talks about refusal for not giving biometrics but did not return the sentence verbatim. Secondhand from a canada.ca IEC page summary: a BIL can arrive 'within 24 hours of applying' if the biometrics fee is paid online with the application.

appointments.application: Ireland first-time registration of an immigration permission (Irish Residence Permit, IRP), non-EEA/UK/Swiss staying over 90 days
appointments.authority: Immigration Service Delivery (ISD), Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration; Burgh Quay Registration Office, 13-14 Burgh Quay, Dublin 2 (took over from GNIB on 2025-01-13)
appointments.waived: Under-16s do not register (they register on turning 16). Renewals and stamp changes are online only, not by appointment.
appointments.feeBasis: Separate fee paid at the appointment by card (no cash): 'The standard registration fee is €300.' Booking is free: 'You do not have to pay a fee to book an appointment ... there are no costs involved in booking an appointment to register.' Whether the fee applies 'will depend on the type of permission you have been given.'
appointments.missed: 'You must register your permission within 90 days of arriving in Ireland.' The landing stamp instructs registration within 90 days. 'If an appointment is not available within 90 days of your arrival, please do not worry. Once you have successfully booked an appointment within the 90 days of arrival, this will be sufficient to remain in the state until the date of your appointment.' Appointments can be moved 'to any other available date at any time via the reschedule option'. A visa-required national who leaves before the appointment cannot re-enter without a new entry visa. The pages read do not state a penalty for not registering at all.
appointments.note: Booking horizon: 'Appointment slots are released on a rolling 90 day basis' and 'appointment slots do fill up quickly'; appointments cannot be booked before arrival, only through the ISD Customer Service Portal. The visit takes 'no longer than 30 minutes' (first-time page) or '60 minutes' (FAQ); photo and fingerprints taken; IRP card posted 'within 10 working days'. Renewal: apply from 12 weeks before IRP expiry (earlier applications refused); no reminders sent. First-time page: https://www.irishimmigration.ie/registering-your-immigration-permission/how-to-register-your-immigration-permission-for-the-first-time/information-on-registering-your-immigration-permission-for-the-first-time/ (updated 2025-01-10).

notFound: US consular interview: travel.state.gov and usembassy.gov blocked automated reads (403/Cloudflare); interview-waiver categories, MRV fees (185/205) and the 365-day fee-receipt validity are secondhand from search summaries of those pages. No single lead time: wait times are published per post.
US: what a consulate does after a no-show (new DS-160 and new fee) was found only on third-party pages, not on an official page.
USCIS: how many days before the ASC appointment the I-797C biometrics notice is sent is not published on the biometrics page or in Policy Manual Vol. 1 Part C Ch. 2.
USCIS O-1 / I-129: no beneficiary biometrics step on the page; in-US change-of-status beneficiaries not covered.

UK: gov.uk does not publish UKVCAS appointment prices; the 'free at core service points' and GBP 69.99 enhanced-point figures are secondhand. Overseas VAC prices and any overseas booking deadline were not found.

Canada: the exact canada.ca sentence that an application is refused for biometrics not given within 30 days was seen only in search summaries; the where-to-give page states only the 30 days and the extension web form.
Ireland: no published penalty for failing to register at all; the 30 vs 60 minute visit length differs between two ISD pages.
